# SPD-060 — Bash hook: a named coproc (coproc NAME compound) hides its group from the hook

## Brief
Found by Spud reviewing SPD-054 with main's module and the branch's: `coproc NAME { git push; }` is read as kinds other with no finding, while `coproc { git push; }`, `coproc git push`, `coproc ( git push )` and `coproc sh -c 'git push'` each find the git push. bash 4 and later accept a name before the compound command (`coproc NAME compound`) and run the group in a forked shell, so a member's VCS write inside it would run under a word the hook takes for the command. zsh has no named form (its coproc takes the command only) and bash 3.2, this Mac's /bin/bash and sh, has no coproc at all, so nothing runs here today; a newer bash on PATH (Homebrew) would. Probe first in whatever bash 4+ is installed, then read the group after an optional NAME word exactly as the unnamed form is read, fail closed on a NAME that holds an expansion.

Evidence: scratchpad script check_coproc.py at SPD-054's session, loading `git show main:bin/spud_ledger.py` and the branch's bin/spud_ledger.py: both print `coproc NAME { git push; } kinds=other findings=[]`.

## Size, persona and model decision
Batch plan v2, wave 1 with SPD-061 and SPD-059, same engineer on opus. The coproc branch is in shell/analyse.py's prefix loop and shell/walk.py. No bash 4+ on this Mac; the probe runs bash 5 in the ubuntu:24.04 podman image already pulled.
